Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the Kiwi reply! The two umpires make their way back as Andy Balbirnie leads his side in a huddle before taking the field. The overhead conditions have gotten a little heavy again which should help the pacers. Martin Guptill and Finn Allen are set to open the innings for New Zealand. Mark Adair to start proceedings with the ball for Ireland.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, Ireland have a decent total on the board but it isn't the one that will bother the Kiwis much. Having said that, the pitch isn't the easiest to bat on, and given the fragility of the Kiwi top order we saw in the other game, this could be a low-scoring thriller. Find out how the chase goes after the break.

George Dockrell is up for a quick chat. Says that he is happy with his innings. Adds that he came out to bat in a tricky situation and had a chat with Lorcan Tucker and they tried to keep the runs flowing in order to put up a decent total. Shares that the pitch is offering turn and it is difficult to bat on but he is satisfied with the way he countered that. Hopes that he can spin a web around the Kiwis too.

Ireland had yet another slow start to their innings and once again the experienced opening pair of Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie was to blame for it. This time around, Harry Tector couldn't hang around for much and it was up to George Dockrell and Lorcan Tucker to stitch together a stand. Dockrell proved to be the aggressor and enjoyed his stay at the crease, scoring his career-best 74 runs off just 61 deliveries before getting out at the death. Mark Adair with a blistering cameo took the hosts over the 200-run mark and has given them something to defend.

The Kiwi pacers took full advantage of the overhead conditions and Matt Henry got the new ball to talk as he picked up a couple of early wickets. The debutant, Jacob Duffy gave him good support but went wicketless only to come back later on and pick up his maiden ODI wicket. The pitch had more than enough in it for the spinners and Michael Bracewell and Mitchell Santner both took good advantage of it. Glenn Phillips too chipped in with a wicket. They failed to pick up wickets for a while but got them in the final 10 overs and that is a very good display overall from the visitors.

A decent recovery in the end from Ireland and they have George Dockrell to thank for that. After losing half their side for 85, the hosts have got to 216 runs which gives them an outside chance of winning the game. New Zealand on the other hand will be content with their bowling display and will hope that the batters seal the deal for them.

OUT! Josh Little is run out. Needless from Mark Adair. He could have taken a single and kept strike for the next over. Fuller in length around off, Mark Adair clears his front leg for a big shot but mistimes it in the air towards sweeper cover. It falls safely and they attempt for the second run as Henry Nicholls fires in a flat throw to the bowler. Matt Henry takes the bails off and Josh Little is well short of the crease. Ireland are all out for 216 and have wasted 12 balls.
Too full and around off, Adair forces it down to long off and once again no run is taken.
Yorker around off, Adair digs it out to covers and declines the single.
Mandatory concussion check! Mark Adair is struck on the grill of the helmet and the physio is out to have a look. Everything seems fine and Adair is good to continue.
BANG ON THE HELMET! A sharp bouncer from Matt Henry. Around middle, Mark Adair tries to pull but takes his eyes off the ball. He misses and takes a blow on his helmet.
FOUR! Boom! Ireland are reaching a challenging total on this pitch. Full and around middle, Mark Adair gives it the full whack of his bat and smacks it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
SIX! Adair continues to add vital runs. Width outside off, Mark Adair latches onto it and sends it flying over extra cover for a biggie.
Matt Henry (8-3-29-2) is back on.
Slower one again, on a length around off, this time Little defends it by showing the full face of his bat. 17 from the over!
Short and around off, Josh chases and misses.
Slower one, on a length around off, Adair waits and hits it to deep cover for a run. Two balls to survive for Little.
Wide! Way wide outside off as Duffy tries to stay away from the hitting zone. Mark Adair leaves.
FOUR! 200 comes up for Ireland. Jacob Duffy digs it in short, around middle, Mark Adair steps back and ramps it behind the keeper for a boundary.
FOUR! Width there outside off, Mark Adair flashes his bat hard at it and edges it down to third man for a boundary.
A wide yorker outside off, Mark fails to dig it out.
SIX! Bonus runs for Ireland and it's a no ball as well for overstepping. A length delivery around off, Mark Adair launches it over long off for a biggie.
Shortish and around off, Josh tries to cut but misses.
Josh Little is the last man in for Ireland.

OUT! Caught behind! Flighted and around off, Craig Young tries to defend but it turns away a shade to take the shoulder of his bat. Tom Latham shows good reflexes and grabs a sharp catch. It's going downhill for Ireland again at the backend of the innings.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Latham b Mitchell Santner

Commentary.Commentary: Floated on off, Craig Young blocks it to the off side.
Width there outside off, forced to deep point for a run.
Craig Young is the new man in.

OUT! RUN OUT! Another blow to Ireland as they lose a set batter. Santner fires it short and on middle, Mark Adair turns and hits it straight towards short fine leg. He doesn't want any run and turns his back but Simi Singh keeps on running, without looking at his partner. Simi realizes late and has no chance of returning. Jacob Duffy sends in the throw and Santner does the rest at his end.
Floated and full, around middle, Singh drives it through covers and picks up a single.
Another swing and a miss. Slower one, on a shortish length and outside off, Adair is early into the shot and misses. End of a successful over for the debutant.
Swish and a miss! Short and on middle, Mark backs away and tries to pull but it goes below his bat.
Thwacked. Fuller and around off, Singh drills it down to long off for one.
Mark Adair is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! A maiden ODI wicket for Jacob Duffy on debut and it is a big one too! This is a bit shorter and around middle, Duffy takes the pace off the ball. George Dockrell backs away looking to club it over the mid-wicket fence but is undone by the lack of pace. Dockrell swings early and mistimes it in the air towards long on. Michael Bracewell over there takes a simple catch and a brilliant knock from Dockrell comes to an end.
Commentary.Howout: c Michael Bracewell b Jacob Duffy

Commentary.Commentary: Walks forward to a length ball and slams it down to long off for a single.
Full and outside off, George Dockrell again tries to attack the first ball of the over but only manages to drag it off the inner edge to deep backward square leg. They cross for a run.
Jacob Duffy (7-1-32-0) is back on.
Fuller in length around middle, it's defended. 11 from the over!
Tossed up, on off, Simi brings out the reverse sweep and gets just enough touch to beat Latham behind the stumps. They will get two as the ball races past short third man.
Around off, tapped on the off side for a run.
Full and around off, chipped over extra cover for a couple of runs.
Short and on middle, pulled across the line but straight to short fine leg.

SIX! Out of here. Dockrell is playing a gem. A touch too full this time, around leg, George Dockrell steps back to give himself room and smashes it all the way over long off for a maximum. The 50-run stand comes off.
Back of a length, around off, defended from the back foot.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Blair Tickner takes the pace off this one and delivers it short and outside off. Simi Singh flashes his bat at it but only manages a thick outside edge to the keeper. It's dying in front of Tom Latham who dives across and snaps it inches above the surface. Singh is not going anywhere. The two umpires get together and refer the decision upstairs. The replays show that it's a clean catch. Hang on, the issue seems to be something else. This delivery is going to be called a dead ball as the towel fell off from Blair's back. Tom Latham is seen arguing with the umpire. A very strange incident but this one is as per the rules. The towel hit the ground before the shot was played. Anyway, Simi survives.
On a length and around off, Dockrell drags it off the inner edge to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Much better. A near-yorker around off, George Dockrell is sitting deep inside the crease and manages only to dig it out.

FOUR! Dockrell is turning on the heat! Tickner continues to be short and this time he offers width outside off, George Dockrell latches onto it and whacks it through extra cover for a boundary. No chance for long off.

FOUR! Dockrell has pressed on the accelerator. This is not smart bowling. Short again, around off, sitting up and begging to be hit. Dockrell attacks it with all his power and hammers it over mid-wicket. One bounce and into the fence it goes.
Wide! A bumper down the leg side, Dockrell ducks.
FOUR! Bosh! Short and around middle, George Dockrell steps back to make room and muscles it over mid on for a boundary.

NOT OUT! Loopy delivery, full and around off, Simi draws forward with a big stretch and tries to defend. But the ball lands and spins away to beat his bat. Latham is quick to take the bails off and appeals. The square leg umpire refers it upstairs. The third umpire first checks for the outside edge and it's found to be absent on the UltraEdge. The side-on angle suggests that Simi's back leg slides out of the crease, he tries to put it inside the crease rather than dragging it in. It's touch and go. The third umpire has a look at numerous replays and decides that the bails weren't fully off. Simi Singh survives by the tiniest of margins.

Is that stumped? Tom Latham thinks he has got his man and the umpires have gone upstairs. The catch will be checked too and UltraEdge confirms that there isn't any bat on it. The third umpire then checks the side-on angle and finds that the foot of Simi Singh is just in the air when the bails are taken off but it is very close. It is a question of when the bail is actually dislodged. The third umpire finds that the bail did get dislodged after the foot was grounded and Simi Singh survives.
Slightly short and on middle, Dockrell goes back and punches it down to long on for a single.
Quicker and fuller on middle, George Dockrell gets forward and defends it towards mid-wicket.
Gets off the strike. Eases a full ball down to long on for a run.
Fuller and around off, Simi reverse-sweeps but finds point.
Flatter and on middle, defended from the back foot to covers.
Back of a length, around off and shaping in, Singh plays down from the back foot and dabs it down towards point. They cross.
FIFTY FOR DOCKRELL! His 3rd in ODIs. A valuable knock from him. Fuller and on middle, George Dockrell drives it back past the bowler to long off. A single is taken. He needs to continue till the end.
Blair is not learning. Serves another short ball outside off and it has been cracked past the point fielder for a single.
Tickner delivers it short again, outside off, Singh cuts and beats the point fielder. They get two more runs.
Back of a length, around off, it's punched to sweeper cover for a single. George Dockrell moves to 49.
FOUR! That's some shot from Dockrell. Short in length, around middle, George Dockrell stands back to get on top of the bounce and pulls it thunderously to the deep mid-wicket fence. 150 up!
Wide! Blair Tickner begins with a bouncer down the leg side, George Dockrell tries to pull but misses.
Powerplay 3 time. One extra fielder, i.e. 5 can now be put outside the 30-yard circle till the end of this inning. Blair Tickner is back into the attack now.
Gives it some air this time around middle, turning away a bit. Singh pushes it from his back foot to point.
Quicker and flatter on leg, Singh knocks it short mid-wicket.
Full and on middle, Singh keeps it out.
Floated on off, Singh leans forward and defends it solidly.
Floated on middle, drifting into the pads. George Dockrell flicks it through square leg for a single.
Flatter and quicker on middle, Singh punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Mitchell Santner is back on. 1 for 15 in his 6 overs so far.

FOUR! Brilliant use of the depth of the crease this time by George Dockrell and he is playing a very important knock here for his side. Shorter and a bit quicker, around off. This is punched off the back foot and through covers for a glorious boundary.
Shorter and at the stumps, Singh plays it off the back foot and behind square on the leg side for one.
Just keeping the scoreboard ticking these two at the moment. Around middle, George Dockrell flicks it uppishly but past the man at mid-wicket for a single.
Floated up around off, Singh leans in and drives it towards long off for one more.
Good use of the feet once again from George Dockrell. On middle, Dockrell steps out and knocks it sweetly down to long on for a run.
Slower through the air on off, Singh pushes it off his back foot through covers for a single.
Another bouncer but this time on off, George Dockrell again ducks under it.
Bangs in a bouncer on middle and leg, George Dockrell ducks underneath it.
Short and on middle and leg, Simi Singh pulls it to fine leg for a run.
Back of a length outside off, Simi Singh knocks it to point.
On a length on off, George Dockrell moves across and flicks it through to fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Shot! This is full on off, George Dockrell gives himself some room by going to the leg side and lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Flatter delivery, around off. George Dockrell punches it off the back foot through wide mid off for a run.
This is turning into middle and leg, Simi Singh works it away nicely through mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted and on off, Singh pushes it back towards the bowler.
Simi Singh walks in next.

OUT! CAUGHT! Very soft dismissal and Lorcan Tucker will be disappointed with that. Glenn Phillips just floats this one up on a length and outside off. Tucker backs away, trying to go over extra cover, but ends up just checking his shot. He chips it straight up in the air around the cover region where Blair Tickner takes a dolly of a catch moving across to his right. Phillips gets the breakthrough and seems all pumped up. Ireland have to rebuild yet again.
Commentary.Howout: c Blair Tickner b Glenn Phillips

Commentary.Commentary: Around off, this is pushed away toward covers for a single.

Difficult chance but it has been dropped! Tosses it up on middle, Lorcan Tucker steps out and looks to heave it aerially towards the mid-wicket fence. Tucker ends up mistiming it well in front of square and Henry Nicholls is a bit hesitant coming in from the deep. Nicholls dives in but can't hold on and the batters get a single.

Update - In the ongoing ICC Men's T20 World Cup Qualifier B, Logan van Beek has taken a hat-trick against Hong Kong, the first for the Netherlands in a T20I game. His victims were Nizakat Khan, Scott McKechnie and Ehsan Khan. Hong Kong have got bundled out for just 116 runs and are staring down at their second loss of the tournament.
Pulls his length back a bit on off, getting it to nip back in. George Dockrell tries to play at it but gets hit high on his thigh pad.
Lands it short on middle, George Dockrell ducks under it. Its called a wide for height.
Back of a length on middle, Lorcan Tucker flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
Bangs in a bouncer on middle and leg, Lorcan Tucker ducks under it.
On a length on middle, George Dockrell moves across and works it through square leg for one.
FOUR! Nice shot again. This is on a good length on middle, angling in. George Dockrell makes room and just opens the face of his bat and guides it towards the third man fence for another boundary.
FOUR! Clever shot! Duffy goes for the yorker but bowls a low full toss on middle, George Dockrell picks it up and smashes it towards deep sqaure leg fence for a boundary.
Jacob Duffy starts his second spell with No ball. This is on a length angling down the leg side. George Dockrell offers no shot at it. It's called a no ball for overstepping. Free Hit coming up...

Drinks break! The Kiwi spinners have kept the pressure on the Irish batters who have struggled so far. But George Dockrell has come out with some positive intent and his movement in the crease is proving to be effective. Ireland do have a couple of all-rounders to come but will hope that Tucker and Dockrell bat for as long as possible. New Zealand will be looking to take wickets and bundle out the opposition.
Keeps it full but pushes it a bit wider, Tucker makes room but fails to get it past the man at cover.
Full and at the stumps, this is worked away to mid-wicket for one more.
Leg bye! Sliding on the pads, Lorcan Tucker looks to wrist it away but the ball goes off the pads and rolls towards square leg. They pick up a leg bye.
Dockrell steps out and turns this length ball past the diving man at square leg for a single.
George Dockrell backs away and Glenn Phillips follows him with a quicker delivery. Dockrell adjusts and nudges it out on the leg side.
Flatter delivery, turning into middle and leg. Tucker hangs deep and eases it through mid-wicket for a run.
Good length on outside off, George Dockrell knocks it to point.
SIX! Good cricket by George Dockrell. This is full again on off, George Dockrell moves to the leg side and smokes it over mid off for a biggie.
Good length outside off, Lorcan Tucker plays it with soft hands to the off side and picks up a single.
TOUGH CHANCE! Matt Henry bowls it full outside off, George Dockrell goes for the drive but plays it in the air and it just goes past a diving Martin Guptill at point. They cross for a single.
On a length and on middle, George Dockrell blocks it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Superb shot! This is full and on the stumps, George Dockrell gives himself some room and lofts it over covers for a boundary. This is trademark Dockrell.
A hint of flight, around off, Tucker flicks it towards mid-wicket.
This is pushed through on a shorter length and around off, Tucker can't get it away on the off side.
Quicker delivery, drifting onto the pads. Tucker looks to tickle it away but the ball just clips his pads.
Missed out! A juicy full toss, outside off from Phillips. Lorcan Tucker though creams it straight to the man at extra cover, he will be disappointed with that.
Shorter in length and on off, Dockrell knocks it down to long on and picks up a run.
On middle, George Dockrell uses his feet but whips it straight to the man at mid-wicket.
WIDE! Glenn Phillips begins with a loosener down the leg side, it is left alone for a wide.
Glenn Phillips is introduced into the attack.
Bowls it full and outside off, Lorcan Tucker leans on and defends it off his front foot to mid off.
A bit full this time on middle and leg, George Dockrell flicks it through square leg for a single.
Good length on middle, George Dockrell pushes it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length on off, George Dockrell blocks it from his back foot.
On a length and on off, angling in. George Dockrell knocks it on the off side.
Matt Henry is back for his second spell and starts with a length ball outside off, holding its line. George Dockrell leaves it alone.
A dot to end a fabulous spell of bowling by Michael Bracewell, he finishes with figures of 10-1-26-2! This is floated up on off, Tucker just pushes it back to the bowler.
Shorter in length and around off, this is played off the back foot but straight to cover.
On a length and turning onto the pads, Dockrell moves past the off stump and just works it through square leg for a run.
FOUR! Sweetly timed! George Dockrell moves past his stumps and Michael Bracewell fires it on off, Dockrell slaps it past point and into the fence. Much needed boundary for Ireland.
Flatter this time, around off. Tucker punches it off the back foot down to long off for a single.
This is quicker and angled into the pads. Lorcan Tucker fails to flick it away and gets hit on the pads.
Shortish and around off, Dockrell punches off the back foot but finds point. Maiden!
Fuller and around leg, Dockrell stays leg-side of this delivery and defends it down.
A hint of away spin, around off, George Dockrell tries to defend off the front foot but is beaten.
Loopy and full, around off, George defends it off the front foot.
Santner pushes it quicker through the air, around off, George Dockrell defends it off the back foot.
Flatter and fuller, around middle, defended off the front foot.
Full and around off, Lorcan tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Around middle, George goes back and nudges it to fine leg for a run.
Beaten! Arm ball outside off, Dockrell goes on the back foot, looks to play for the turn but gets beaten as it skids straight on.
Another flick shot but this time it's straight to Guptill at mid-wicket.
Flicks a full ball past the right side of the mid-wicket fielder. They decide not to cross.
Shortish and around off, Tucker goes back and punches it down the ground. It goes through the legs of George Dockrell at the other end and travels to long on. They cross.
Flighted and around off, defended off the front foot to the off side.
Turn and bounce again, around off, George tries to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Fuller and on middle, defended off the front foot.
George Dockrell is in at number 7.

OUT! CAUGHT! This was always on the cards and credit to Tom Latham for persisting with a slip fielder. Smart bowling from Mitchell Santner. There is enough in the pitch and all he needs to do is to land it in good areas. Santner does exactly that. He gives it a good toss, getting the ball to drift in around off, Curtis Campher commits himself on the front foot, attempting to defend but the ball turns away with extra bounce and takes the shoulder of his bat. It flies to first slip where Finn Allen accepts a simple catch. Ireland are in deep trouble with five of their top batters back in the pavilion.
Commentary.Howout: c Finn Allen b Mitchell Santner

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! Turn and bounce from around off, Curtis Campher stands there like a sitting duck, attempting to defend but it beats the outside edge. Unplayable.
A touch short and on off, Lorcan Tucker goes back, allows the ball to spin away and then punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Slower through the air, full and drifting in around off, Campher strides forward and defends it back.
Fuller and close to off, Curtis Campher draws forward and defends it to the off side.
Lunges to a full ball and pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Gets behind the line and pushes it to the right of the bowler.
Full and flighted again, outside off, Curtis inside-edges his attempted drive to short mid-wicket.
Flighted delivery, full and around off, Tucker flicks it through square leg for a run.
Loopy and full, on middle, Campher defends it off the front foot. The Kiwi spinners continue to run through their overs.
Quicker and fuller around middle, Tucker tucks it behind square leg for a run.
Play and a miss! Slower through the air, full and outside off, Lorcan gets back and tries to sweep but it spins away to beat his bat.
Short and on off, Lorcan steps back and slaps it to sweeper cover for two.
Fuller and on middle, defended towards mid-wicket.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and pushes it to covers.
SIX! Once again the over ends with a biggie. Loopy delivery, full and around off, this time Curtis Campher goes down on one knee and powers his slog sweep over mid-wicket.
Fuller and on off, Curtis flicks but finds wide mid on.

Was that a catch? Flighted delivery, full and around off, Curtis Campher goes down to play the reverse-batted sweep shot but there is no connection. It appears to have lobbed from the gloves but the first slip fielder has not caught it over his head. After having a closer look, that might have come off the wrists.
Leans forward to a full ball and dead-bats it on the surface.
A touch short and around off, Curtis sweeps but finds short fine leg.
Fuller and on middle, defended to mid-wicket.
SIX! Sends one into the stands! This shot will release the pressure. Full and floated, outside off, Lorcan Tucker sits down on one knee and smokes it over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Flatter this time, around the pads, Lorcan tucks it to square leg.
Loopy and full, landing outside off, Lorcan Tucker goes down and across to sweep but fails to connect. It goes off his pads to first slip.
Fuller this time, around off, it's driven down to mid off.
Short this time and outside off, Tucker cuts but finds the point fielder.
Flighted and full on middle, Lorcan steps back and defends it down.
Turn and bounce from around off, Curtis Campher tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. Another tidy over.

SAFE! It's a bump ball. Coming to the delivery, it's nicely tossed up, around off and fuller in length, Curtis Campher goes down to slog it across the line but gets an under-edge. It clips his pads and lobs towards first slip where the fielder dives forward to take a low catch. The Kiwi players appeal. The two umpires get together and then decide to refer it upstairs. The soft signal is not out. The replays find that the ball had bounced before brushing the pads.

Is that a bump ball? There is an appeal for a catch but the ball seems to have touched the ground and then went up. The fielder at first slip pouches it but the umpires go upstairs and the soft signal is not out. The replay shows that clearly the ball hit the ground and then went up again off the pads. NOT OUT!
Very full and around off, Lorcan Tucker knocks it down to long on for one.
Extra toss on this delivery, Curtis Campher takes it on the full and drives it down to long off for a run.
Short and on off, Curtis cuts it from the back foot but finds point.
Quicker and fuller on off, defended to the off side.
Tossed up, around off, it's pushed to covers for a quick single.
Floated and full, around off, Curtis Campher lunges and defends it from the inner half of his blade.
Outside off, played down in front of point for a quick run.
Shortish and on middle, Lorcan goes back and turns it to mid-wicket.
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it this time from the middle of the bat.
Beaten comprehensively. Drifting in around middle, Tucker tries to defend but it spins away to beat the outside edge.
Maiden! Quicker and shorter outside off, Curtis Campher tries to cut but misses.
Short and outside off, Curtis cuts it from the outer half but fails to beat Jacob Duffy at short third man.
Well stopped! Around off, flatter through the air, Campher punches it from the back foot and Michael Bracewell makes a diving stop to his left.
Shortish and outside off, Campher moves across the stumps to pull but ends up dragging it back towards the bowler.
Flighted and full, around off, Campher reverse-sweeps but finds cover-point.
Drags his length short and puts it around off, Curtis Campher goes back and punches it to covers.
Tossed up on off, Curtis Campher thrashes it towards sweeper cover for a run.
A bit short outside off, Curtis Campher goes on his back foot and cuts it through cover-point for a brace.
Nicely bowled! Slower and on a length on middle, Campher leans in to defend but gets hit on the gloves.
Flatter and quicker on off, Curtis Campher defends it solidly.
Floated on middle, Curtis Campher blocks it on the off side.
Starts with a beauty. Tossed up on middle, sharply turning away. Curtis Campher tries to play at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Mitchell Santner comes into the attack now.
Nicely tossed up on middle, turning in. Lorcan Tucker leans forward to defend but gets hit on his body. The ball goes in the air but falls safely around the short fine leg region.
A bit short outside off, turning in. Lorcan Tucker punches it to covers.
Slower through the air on middle, Lorcan Tucker knocks it to short mid-wicket.
Lorcan Tucker is the new batter.

OUT! STUMPED! Smart bowling from Michael Bracewell and the well-set Andy McBrine departs! McBrine pre-meditates and decides to use his feet. Bracewell sees the batter coming down the track and just flights it outside off, with the ball turning away as well. McBrine gets nowhere near the pitch of the ball and Tom Latham is lightning quick behind the stumps to whip off the bails. Ireland lose their fourth and McBrine is disgusted with himself.
Commentary.Howout: st Tom Latham b Michael Bracewell

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on middle, Curtis Campher goes down and sweeps it through square leg for a single.
Floated outside off, Curtis Campher pushes it to covers.
Around the top of off, this is played late and nicely guided towards third man for a single.
A bit of extra bounce on this occasion! This is on a good length and angling into middle and leg, Campher looks to defend but is a bit surprised by the bounce and gets hit on the gloves.
Back of a length, angling across off, McBrine stays back and steers it down to third man for a run.
Effort ball from Blair Tickner, digs it in short and around off. The ball rises really high and Curtis Campher does well to play a controlled pull shot down to deep square leg for one.
Back of a length, angling in from middle and into the body. Campher looks to fend it away but fails to do so.
On a length and around off, just a bit slower too. Campher plays it late and with soft hands down to backward point.
Full and on middle, Andy McBrine tries to sweep but gets an inside edge towards square leg.
Darts in a yorker on middle, Andy McBrine digs it out well.
Full and outside off, Campher drills it towards covers where there is a misfield and they get a single.
Tossed up outside off, Curtis Campher drives it through covers for a brace.
FOUR BYES! Floated on off stump and turning in, Campher goes for the paddle sweep but misses and the ball goes over the stumps and past the keeper for a boundary.
Tossed up on off, turning in. Campher blocks it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Great timing! This is full and on off, Andy McBrine drives it through covers for another boundary. 50 up for Ireland!
Pulls his length back a bit on middle, Andy McBrine knocks it to square leg.
Short again outside off, Andy McBrine gets on top of the bounce and blocks it out.
Back of a length on middle, angling in. Andy McBrine dabs it to mid-wicket.
WIDE! Lands it short and way outside off, Andy McBrine slashes his bat at it but could not connect. It's called a wide.
Full and on middle and leg, Curtis Campher works it through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Nicely played! Blair Tickner bowls it short outside off, and Curtis Campher cuts it hard past backward point for a boundary.

Drinks break. New Zealand have dominated the game so far. They started well with the ball in the last ODI also but failed to maintain the same pressure in the middle overs. This time around, they appear to be better prepared, although having one less pace bowler on this surface could be playing in Latham's mind. Anyway, the Kiwis have a strong hold at the moment and removing Harry Tector cheaply would have eased half of their tension. Michael Bracewell is getting the ball to spin, so with Mitchell Santner around too, New Zealand will aim to keep the upper hand. Can Ireland string a partnership or two to recover from this precarious position? Let's find out.
Another inside edge! This is flatter and turning in from outside off, Curtis Campher looks to drive but gets an inside edge past the stumps and towards fine leg. Just a single this time around.
Flighted this time, outside off, this is stroked away to the man at cover-point.
Flatter this time, around off. Kept out by Campher.

How did that miss the leg stump? Michael Bracewell bowls this one a bit quicker and around off, the ball turns in sharply and a mile too. Curtis Campher gets an inside edge that goes inches past the leg stump and down to fine leg. They pick up a couple of runs.
Bracewell pushes it a bit wider and McBrine goes after it. He slashes it over point and picks up a single.
Fuller and on off, from around the wicket. Andy McBrine solidly defends it out.
Tickner gets his line tighter to the off pole and keeps it on a good length, Campher punches it out towards cover.
Short of a good length and a bit wider outside off, Campher has thrown his hands at it but gets beaten for pace.
On a good length and on the fifth stump line. Curtis Campher lets it through to the keeper.

TWO WIDES! Another wild delivery from Blair Tickner and thankfully for him, Tom Latham gets a glove on it. This is angled down leg and going further down, Latham dives and gets a glove on it as the ball goes towards fine leg. The batters cross for a single as well.
Much better! Good length, angling into off, McBrine defends it out from his crease.
WIDE! Good take from Tom Latham behind the stumps. This is a poor delivery, angled way down the leg side and Latham had to spring to his right to pouch it.
Back of a length and around off, this is dabbed down towards backward point.
WIDE! A huge grunt once again from Tickner as he tries to angle this short ball at the body but spills it down the leg side, wide called.

Ouch, that must have stung! Tickner comes from around the wicket to the left-hander and angles in a short ball on off. Andy McBrine tries to fend it away but gets hurried on and gets a blow flush on the left bicep.
Flatter delivery, around off and this is pushed away towards cover-point. End of a successful first over from Michael Bracewell, just a single and a wicket off it.
Around off again, just holding it back a touch this time. Campher plays it out with soft hands.
This is pushed through quicker and around off, Campher pushes it out towards covers.
Curtis Campher walks in next.

OUT! CAUGHT! A huge, huge wicket for the Kiwis and the centurion from the last game is gone! Michael Bracewell tosses it up on the middle stump line, Harry Tector dances down the track and tries to hit it with the spin. But he doesn't get to the pitch of the ball and ends up forcing it off the toe end of the bat. The ball flies straight to the man at long on and Glenn Phillips over there takes a simple catch. Bracewell with a wicket in his first over and New Zealand are in the driving seat.
Commentary.Howout: c Glenn Phillips b Michael Bracewell

Commentary.Commentary: On a nagging length, turning it in from outside off. Tector defends it off the back foot.
Starts off with a loopy delivery around off, Andy McBrine cuts it hard and towards deep point for just a single.
Time for Michael Bracewell to do some magic with the ball. A slip in place.

End of an excellent first over from Blair Tickner, a maiden. This is on a hard length, on a tighter line around off too. Tector hangs on the back foot to defend it out but gets beaten past the outside edge again.
Length ball, around off, Tector presses forward and defends it out on the off side.
BEATEN! Pitches it up this time, in the channel around off and the ball just holds its line. Harry Tector is on the front foot, looking to block but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Back of a length, around off. Tector punches it off the back foot but straight to the man at cover-point.
Tickner grunts and delivers a short ball outside off, Harry Tector leaves it alone with ease.

Tickner starts off with a fullish delivery around off and gets a bit of shape in the air. Tector looks to drive it through covers but gets it off the inner half of the bat. The ball rolls away to mid-wicket.
Blair Tickner comes in as the first bowling change.
Keeps it around the top of off, McBrine blocks it out on the off side.

FOUR! Well, the sun is out and the boundaries are flowing here for Ireland! Matt goes a bit fuller, Andy McBrine just takes a couple of steps towards the ball and punches it gloriously past the man at mid off for the third boundary in the over.
Good length, over middle stump, McBrine hops back and defends it out.
FOUR! No luck in that shot, Andy McBrine has muscled it! Just a fraction short and over off, McBrine rocks back and pulls it past square leg for a boundary.
Length, around the top of off, McBrine solidly keeps it out.

EDGED AND FOUR! Matt Henry almost picks up the third wicket but Andy McBrine gets lucky. This is fuller and angling across the left-hander, McBrine looks for the cover drive but gets a thick outside edge that flies past the man at first slip and into the vacant third man fence.
Powerplay 2! The fielding side can now have a maximum of 4 fielders outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over.
Short and on off, defended from the crease to the off side. Powerplay 1 is done, it's a great one for the Kiwis.
Around off, on a length, Andy McBrine plays it down with soft hands and steals a quick run.
Wide! Short but down the leg side, Andy gets across and leaves it alone.
The batter has just blocked that from his crease.

FOUR! Shot of the day so far and this will make Andy McBrine feel a lot better. The crowd is also very appreciative. Fuller in length and around off, McBrine leans into the drive and caresses it through the gap at covers.
On a length, around off, pushed back to the bowler.

Direct hit but no harm is done. Shortish and around off, Harry Tector goes on the back foot and taps it down towards covers. He sets off for a single and completes it safely as Glenn Phillips scores a direct hit at the bowler's end.
Connects with one and finds the gap. Back of a length, around off, Andy punches it through extra cover and picks up a couple.
Beaten again! Henry takes a length ball away from the left-hander, outside off, McBrine flashes his blade at it and misses.
Andy McBrine is struggling at the moment. Back of a length, around off, Andy swings his bat at it but connects only with thin air.
Helps a length ball on the leg side but fails to find the gap. Straight to mid-wicket.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and drives it down to mid on.
Play and a miss! A touch short in length and outside off, Andy McBrine walks down the track and throws his bat at it but fails to connect.
On a length and outside off, moving away, Tector lets it be. Probing over.

OUCH! Jacob Duffy hits the deck hard and extracts some extra bounce. It shoots up from a good length around off, Harry Tector tries to defend but it climbs to smash him on the gloves. Tector immediately pulls out in pain.
Shortish and on off, defended from the back foot to the off side.
Edged but wide of the slip cordon. Another outswinger that squares up the batter in defense. This time the ball takes the outside edge and runs down to third man. They pick up a couple of runs.
Beautiful! A hint of away movement there, from a length around off, Harry Tector is opened up in defense as the ball whistles past the outside edge.

A touch short around leg, shaping in, Andy McBrine initially tries to glance but then pulls his bat away. It goes off his thigh pad to the leg side and they cross. We all thought it would be given as a dead ball but umpire Aleem Dar signals for a leg bye. Hmm...
The line from Henry becomes a little too straight and this time Harry helps it with soft hands to mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, Harry Tector is nicely forward on this occasion as he defends it to the off side.

A muted appeal for an lbw! Inswinger from Henry again. On a fuller length around off, Harry Tector tries to defend but gets an INSIDE EDGE onto the pads. A similar delivery got Paul Stirling out. Tector is in form so he managed some bat behind it.
Movement off the deck with extra bounce. Around middle, Harry Tector walks forward to work it around the corner but misses and takes a blow near the groin area. That would have hurt.
Angling in from a length around off, Harry Tector covers the line and defends it to the off side. Looking assured at the crease. This is what good form does to you.
Short in length and outside off, Harry Tector shoulders arms.
Touch fuller and on middle, this is pushed gently towards mid on.
Back of a length, around middle and this one nips back in off the surface. Andy McBrine tries to tuck it away but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
A touch shorter in length and outside off, Harry Tector plays at it with soft hands and edges it down past the slip cordon. The ball goes to third man and a single is taken.
On a good length and around off, Tector leaves this one through to the keeper.
Back of a length and outside off, McBrine plays it off the back foot and past backward point for a single.
This is full and swinging into the pads of Andy McBrine who tries to flick but falls over and gets hit on the pads.
Tector covers the line this time and defends it towards mid off.
Back of a length, around off and shaping away, Harry Tector feels for it inside the line and misses.
Harry Tector is the new man in.

OUT! LEFT ALONE AND BOWLED! Yet again both the Irish openers have been sent packing cheaply. Matt Henry was exceptional in the last game with the new ball and he has hit the right chords here as well. A lovely inswinger. It lands on a good length around off and nips back in after kissing the deck. Andy Balbirnie decides not to offer any shot and lifts his bat up to make way for the ball through to the keeper. But to his disappointment, the ball keeps on moving and goes on to clip the top of the off stump. A dream delivery. Matt Henry celebrates calmly. The other fast bowlers would have gone bonkers after claiming a wicket in this manner.
Shortish and on off, defended off the back foot.
Aerial but wide of point! A length ball around off, Andy McBrine tries to drive off the front foot but slices it past the diving point fielder. A single is taken.

Angles a length ball into the batter, Andy Balbirnie works it gently towards mid on and rushes towards the other end. The fielder comes up with a direct hit at the bowler's end but Balbirnie is safely in.
Halt in play! There is some issue with one of the stump mics and it is hanging out. The stumps are being removed and the stump mic is being put back in place correctly.
Shortish and on off, defended from the back foot.
WIDE! Way wide outside off, the batter leaves.
An inswinging yorker around leg, McBrine keeps it out safely beside the pitch.

Beautiful delivery. Jacob Duffy is known for his outswingers to the right-handers. Andy McBrine, being a left-hander, gets this one to nip back in. It's a touch short around middle and Andy McBrine is beaten on the inside edge as he attempts to defend from the crease. This one is called a no ball for overstepping.
A bit short and outside off, Andy McBrine goes on the back foot and taps it down to covers.
IRELAND ARE OFF THE MARK! Fuller in length, around middle, Andy Balbirnie flicks it to the right of mid on where Mitchell Santner misfields slightly and allows the home team to open its account.
Shortish and on middle, Andy Balbirnie goes on the back foot and plays it towards wide mid on.
A gentle outswinger, in the channel outside off, Andy Balbirnie stays back to guard his stumps as he leaves.
Make it three maidens in a row! Fuller in length and close to off, Andy McBrine presses forward and blocks it on the pitch.
Well struck but not in the gap. Fuller and on off, Andy McBrine drives it off the front foot but finds mid off.
A touch short and outside off, Andy McBrine tries to punch but mistimes his shot to the off side.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and offers a straight bat in defense.
Close to off, on a good length, again McBrine is behind the line and this time he blocks it well.
Shortish and on off, Andy McBrine goes on his toes and defends it down from the bottom part his blade.
Bowls it on a good length around off, once again the Irish skipper goes on the back foot as he defends it down. Two maidens in a row from the Black Caps.
Slightly short this time, around off, Andy Balbirnie climbs on the back foot and plays it down safely to cover-point.
A little bit of away shape from a fuller length around off, Andy Balbirnie pushes it away tentatively towards the cover region.
Full this time, angling in around off, Balbirnie gets behind the line and blocks.
Another delivery outside off, Balbirnie shows no interest in playing at it.
Jacob Duffy begins with a good-length delivery, outside off, Andy Balbirnie makes a leave.
The ODI debutant, Jacob Duffy to take the other new ball.
Back of a length, around off and angling away, Andy McBrine allows it through to the keeper. Matt Henry begins with a wicket maiden.
Around off, on a length, it's defended to the off side.
Andy McBrine walks in at number 3.

OUT! PLUMB IN FRONT! A 4-ball duck for the Irish opener. Matt Henry spears it in, on a fuller length and in line with the stumps. Paul Stirling is beaten for pace and movement. He shows very little front foot movement as the ball seams back in to ping him on the pads. The appeal is made, the finger goes up and Paul Stirling immediately walks. He knows that his destiny has been written.
Delivers it on a good length and outside off, Paul Stirling gives a bit of charge and then makes a leave.
Pitches it up this time, full and around middle, Paul Stirling defends it gently towards mid-wicket.
Henry begins well. Lands it on a fuller length outside off, Stirling covers the line and shoulders arms. There is a nice carry to the keeper.

We are ready for the start of play! The two umpires are out in the middle and the crowd is filling in as well. The New Zealand team is seen in a huddle before they walk out to play. The Kiwi players are wearing black armbands to mark the demise of former captain Barry Sinclair who passed away at the age of 85. Paul Stirling and the skipper, Andy Balbirnie are the openers for Ireland. Matt Henry has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Andy Balbirnie, the Irish skipper, says that he would have preferred to bowl as well. He says that they will continue to play as they did in the first game and look to improve in some areas. He adds there is not much time to settle in when playing three matches against a top team like New Zealand. Informs that they are playing the same team.

Tom Latham, the Kiwi captain, says that they want to bowl due to the overhead conditions. Adds that the pitch looks soft and they will look to make early inroads. Praises Bracewell's knock in the last game and hopes for more partnerships in this game. Feels that they are almost there with the ball and tells that on this small ground, it's difficult to defend. Wants his team to take the learnings from the last match. Informs that Mitchell Santner has recovered and replaces Ish Sodhi while Lockie Ferguson gets replaced by Jacob Duffy who will make his debut.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Martin Guptill, Finn Allen, Will Young, Tom Latham (C/WK), Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips, Michael Bracewell, Matt Henry, Blair Tickner, Mitchell Santner (In for Ish Sodhi) and Jacob Duffy (On debut) (In for Lockie Ferguson).
Ireland (Unchanged XI) - Paul Stirling, Andy Balbirnie (C), Andy McBrine, Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, Lorcan Tucker (WK), George Dockrell, Mark Adair, Simi Singh, Craig Young and Josh Little.
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and they will have a BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Kyle McCallan is pitchside. He says that the pitch is a bit damp due to the overnight rain and there's a nice even covering of grass. Adds that out of the 17 completed ODIs here, the captain winning the toss hardly ever decides to bat first and the general notion will be to bowl first.
